sources.title: Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch: the former Liquor Control and Licensing Branch, renamed (5 July 2018)
Hansard, 1 September 1977: the Liquor Distribution Branch and Liquor Control and Licensing Branch budgets separated
Skilled Trades BC Act, s. 42: the Industry Training Appeal Board continued as the Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board
OIC 650/2022: Skilled Trades BC Act in force 1 December 2022

first_observed.meaning: Shown, as the Liquor Control and Licensing Branch, with its budget separated from the Liquor Distribution Branch's from 1 April 1977. The same branch: the 2018 bulletin calls it the former LCLB, renamed. A sighting, not its start
first_observed.locator: Hansard, 1 September 1977, answer of Hon. K.R. Mair to question 97, pp. 5210-5211

research_events.summary: Described as the former Liquor Control and Licensing Branch, renamed the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch
research_events.meaning: The rename had happened by this day; its effective day is not established

records.note: Integration review §3 (claims R3F-C-0204, R3F-C-0265): the identity bridge from the LCLB is explicit; the exact renaming day is open.

review.scope: Identity bridge only; not a complete lifecycle

research_events.summary: The Industry Training Appeal Board continued as the Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board under s. 42 of the Skilled Trades BC Act
research_events.meaning: A continuation under a new name, not a dissolution and a new board: the Act came into force that day (OIC 650/2022)
research_events.locator: Skilled Trades BC Act, SBC 2022 c. 4, s. 42; in force by OIC 650/2022

review.scope: Identity bridge only; not a complete lifecycle
